title: The nitrogen cycle
caption: Most organisms cannot use N₂ because its triple bond is so strong. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria turn it into ammonium; nitrifying bacteria turn ammonium into nitrate (by way of nitrite); plants assimilate nitrate into protein and DNA; decomposers return nitrogen from dead matter as ammonium; and denitrifying bacteria turn nitrate back into N₂ in waterlogged soil.
alt: A ring of six nitrogen stores: atmospheric nitrogen, ammonium, nitrate, plants, animals and dead matter, joined by arrows for nitrogen fixation, nitrification, assimilation, feeding, death and excretion, ammonification and denitrification.
description: Nitrogen fixation: bacteria (Rhizobium, Azotobacter) or lightning turn N₂ into ammonia, which forms ammonium.
Nitrification: Nitrosomonas turns ammonium into nitrite and Nitrobacter turns nitrite into nitrate.
Assimilation: plants absorb nitrate to make proteins and DNA; animals get nitrogen by feeding.
Death and excretion pass nitrogen to dead matter; ammonification by decomposers turns it back into ammonium.
Denitrification: anaerobic bacteria turn nitrate back into N₂.
